slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Only copy evidenced. Written by FUN_080e69bc via FUN_080f1e1c to SRAM 0x0E000000; bytes 0x6188..0x7FFF are untouched 0xFF in the populated sample so no backup/mirror exists there. Exact write length is inferred from the 0xFF tail start (0x6188) because the length literal _DAT_080e69dc is unresolved. Boot acceptance gated by FUN_080e0ee0 (8-byte compare + checksum_1 validate); no generation counter or A/B selection found.

checksums.name: checksum_1
checksums.formula_detail: u=SEED; for each u16_le w in region: u=((u+w)&0xFFFF)^K; stored u16 compared in FUN_080e692c and written by FUN_080e697c. Decompiled form: uVar1=((*puVar2+uVar1)*0x10000 ^ _DAT_080e68f0)>>0x10 over ushorts from _DAT_080e68e8 for _DAT_080e68ec bytes, seed _DAT_080e68e4. SEED, K=(_DAT>>16), start, length and stored offset are unresolved literal-pool values (ROM not in workspace), so no numeric verification was possible. Plain sum16/xor16/crc16/crc32 over candidate ranges and recurrence brute-force (seed 0, all K) over the deck-like region all failed to match candidate stored values.

open_questions: Checksum seed, XOR constant K, covered ranges and stored offsets for both checksums are unresolved literal-pool values (_DAT_080e68e4/68e8/68ec/68f0, _DAT_080e691c/6920/6924/6928, base+off pairs in 0x080e692c/6954/697c/699c); the ROM is not in the workspace, so they cannot be read and no checksum could be verified on samples. Resolution path: report section 6 Steps A-B (self-repair diffing + recurrence solving), or supply the ROM literal pool at 0x080e68e4..0x080e69dc.

Is YUGIOHGX at 0x384E the save magic compared by FUN_080e0ee0, or a deck/player name? Its context (u16 0x1A before, candidate checksum 0x6CFD, count 40, 40 u16s after) supports the name reading. Discriminated by fuzzing target 1.
Exact SRAM write length (slot size): inferred 0x6188 from the 0xFF tail, but _DAT_080e69dc is unresolved; a larger length writing 0x00/0xFF trailing bytes cannot be excluded from one sample.

RAM base address of the save struct (EWRAM 0x02000000 vs IWRAM) and all struct offsets expressed as base+_DAT are unresolved; only +0x6180 is literal in code. Locating YUGIOHGX in emulator RAM after load would resolve the base.
Who calls the SRAM read (0x080f1ce4), the validity gate (0x080e0ee0) and checksum_2 validator (0x080e6954)? No traced callers - edges are hidden by unrecovered jumptables or untraced code.

Only one populated sample exists (plus one blank), although PACKET.md mentions 6 .sav files; no differential field tracking across gameplay states was possible. PACKET.md profile also claims candidate_checksum_or_counter_spans empty and classification multi_state_mutated_save, which the workspace files alone cannot reproduce.
Gameplay semantics of all record arrays (stride-12 region, stride-8 sorted table, sparse u16 arrays, trailing scalars at 0x6148..0x6184) are unknown; no third-party data was used to label them.

FUN_080e69bc discards the result of the checksum_1 validation before flushing (likely a decompiler jumptable artefact); whether a failed validation actually blocks the write in the real code is unconfirmed.
